meta.title: OpenPlanner – video appointments with your team, booked in seconds
meta.description: OpenPlanner is the open-source scheduler for video calls on Webex. Participants pick a free time on a page in your branding, the call lands in Webex Contact Center, and personal data is gone 24 hours after the call.

hero.lead: OpenPlanner is the scheduler for video calls on Webex. A participant picks a free time on a page in your branding, gets a confirmation with a calendar invite and joins from the browser. No account, no app, no login. Your team receives the call at the right moment in Webex Contact Center, and personal data is gone 24 hours after the call.

demo.lead: A real appointment page, without the real appointment. Everything works by keyboard. Nothing is stored or sent.

tour.title: From click to call, in thirty seconds
tour.lead: An animated impression of the chain: the participant books, Webex creates the meeting, the work item drops into the team's queue, and the first free agent picks up.

steps.title: The participant books
steps.text: Month calendar, free times of the day, a short form. On your domain, in your branding.

steps.title: Webex creates the meeting
steps.text: Every appointment is its own Webex meeting. The confirmation carries the calendar invite and the link to reschedule.

steps.title: The work item lands with the team
steps.text: Five minutes before the start, the call goes to the queue in Webex Contact Center as a work item.

steps.title: The first free agent picks up
steps.text: The agent sees a first name and a subject, nothing more, and joins the call as cohost.

tour.video_title: Screen recording of the real interface
tour.video_text: On every release the pipeline records the booking flow and the agenda again, so what you see here is what you install.

steps.title: You set up a group
steps.text: A team is a group: opening hours, staffing per block, holidays, exceptions, texts and branding. All in the admin portal, no code.

steps.title: Your website links to the page
steps.text: Every group has its own page on your domain. Or you place the calendar as a Web Component right inside your own site.

steps.title: The call arrives by itself
steps.text: As a work item in Webex Contact Center, or soon through the built-in queue or a calendar invite for teams without a contact center.

features.title: Everything a call needs, nothing that distracts
features.lead: Built for teams that serve many people by video: customer service, advisory desks, intake, helpdesks.

items.title: Booking without friction
items.text: Month calendar, free times, three fields. Move or cancel through a personal link. Works without JavaScript and fully by keyboard.

items.title: Webex built in
items.text: Every appointment gets its own Webex meeting. The participant joins from the browser, no app or account; your team joins as cohost.

items.title: Lands where your team works
items.text: The call goes to the queue in Webex Contact Center as a work item. The first free agent picks up. Nobody has to watch a calendar.

items.title: Talk now
items.text: A group that is open can offer a direct call, with a cap on the number waiting and honest queue feedback.

items.title: Privacy by design
items.text: Personal data lives only on the booking and is gone 24 hours after the call. Never in logs, URLs, jobs or error messages.

items.title: Your brand, your words
items.text: Colours, logo and font per organisation. Every text editable in the portal. Dutch and English out of the box, more locales possible.

items.title: Messages that arrive
items.text: Confirmation, change, reminder and cancellation by email (with .ics) and SMS. SPF, DKIM and DMARC are checked for you.

items.title: Agenda and planner
items.text: Admins follow every call live, plan staffing per block and close a group in one action when needed, after which participants pick a new time themselves.

integrations.title: Webex Meetings is the heart. Everything else connects to it.
integrations.lead: OpenPlanner is not a video platform and not a contact center. It is the scheduler that ties together the Webex products you already have, and keeps every other system behind a clean adapter.

items.name: Webex Meetings
items.text: Every appointment is a real Webex meeting through the Meetings API. Browser-direct join, a trial call beforehand, live meeting status in the agenda.

items.name: Webex Contact Center
items.text: Five minutes before the start the call becomes a work item in the team's queue, through the Tasks API, carrying only a first name, the join link and routing attributes. Direct call and queue cap included.

items.name: Webex Messaging
items.text: A bot tells administrators in Webex when the integration falters, a queue fills up or a check fails. Never personal data, always a link to the portal.

items.name: Your identity provider
items.text: Administrators sign in through your own IdP (PingFederate, Keycloak, Entra ID, any OIDC provider), per organisation, with roles from the claims.

items.name: Email and SMS
items.text: SMTP and a provider-neutral SMS gateway per organisation. Texts per channel and per group editable in the portal.

items.name: AI agents and bots
items.text: A contact-center bot (such as the Webex AI Agent) asks for free times and books on the participant's behalf through an API with scopes and per-client keys.

integrations.roadmap: A built-in queue or calendar invite for teams without a contact center (ADR 0043), changes through the bot API (ADR 0023), staff through SCIM (ADR 0046), and a provider-neutral contact-center layer (ADR 0032).

enterprise.title: Enterprise-ready from the first commit
enterprise.lead: The first client is a government contact center. You see that in every line of the pipeline.

items.title: One authorisation matrix
items.text: Role × permission × level in one place. Every admin route declares one permission, every query filters by scope, every denial is in the audit log. No exception for superusers.

items.title: Single sign-on, no detour
items.text: OIDC with PKCE, state and nonce, asymmetric algorithms only, eight-hour session. No local accounts, no break-glass login, on purpose.

items.title: An audit log you can forward
items.text: Logins, changes and denials as structured events, to syslog, Splunk or Elastic. Without personal data.

items.title: Signed releases
items.text: Images signed keyless with cosign, an SBOM (CycloneDX) on every release, CVE scans with trivy and grype, hashes in the lockfile. The installation verifies the signature.

items.title: A strict pipeline
items.text: mypy strict, ruff, bandit, semgrep, gitleaks, mutation testing, schemathesis, OWASP ZAP, Playwright with axe-core and Lighthouse. Everything blocks the merge.

items.title: Light to run
items.text: Two containers, one SQLite file, HTTPS with automatic certificates or your own proxy. Updates and release channel from the portal. The backup is one file.

items.title: Accessible, provably
items.text: WCAG 2.2 AA on every public page, in every language, tested again on every pull request. No time limits, no CAPTCHA puzzles.

items.title: Configurable, not hard-coded
items.text: Every threshold, limit and period is a setting with a class, a default and bounds. What is a protection cannot be switched off from the portal.

opensource.title: Open source, open decisions
opensource.lead: OpenPlanner is published under the EUPL-1.2, the open-source licence of the European Commission. Not only the code is open: every design decision sits in the repository as an ADR, with what has been built of it.

points.title: EUPL-1.2
points.text: Use, change and distribute it, commercially too. Compatible with GPL, AGPL and most European procurement rules.

points.title: Architecture Decision Records
points.text: More than eighty decisions, each with context, choice, settings and build status. You read why things are the way they are, and what does not run yet.

points.title: Security up front
points.text: A threat model per flow, an abuse case per endpoint, each with a test. Responsible disclosure through SECURITY.md.

points.title: Contributions welcome
points.text: Issues, discussions and pull requests on GitHub. A CLA keeps the licence clean. Every PR answers the same seven review questions.

releases.title: Releases
releases.lead: Every merge to main becomes a release candidate on the rc channel. A release is a signed image, an SBOM and this website, in one train.

cta.title: Put it on a test server this afternoon
cta.text: One install script, a Let's Encrypt certificate and a demo group. Or start locally with docker compose and walk the portal as every role.

footer.tagline: Video appointments with your team, booked in seconds, privacy by default.
